figure: Figure 11.1 (Discrete vs continuous batching, Orca-style slot diagram)
issue: Grayscale distinguishability of the shared legend. The 'idle slot (bubble)' and 'admission event (backfill)' swatches are both encoded as hatching plus color (pink vs green). In a grayscale print the two hatched swatches collapse to similar gray textures and the color cue is lost; the legend is the only place the two hatched categories sit side by side, so a print reader cannot reliably map them without color.
evidence: Top legend row shows a pink hatched swatch next to a green hatched swatch; at 150 dpi no clear line-style or shape difference separates the two hatches, and the in-panel pink 'idle' fill does not obviously match the legend swatch pattern.
acceptance_test: In a grayscale render the idle and admission legend swatches are distinguishable by pattern or shape (e.g., dots vs diagonal hatch, or a distinct border style), not by color alone; and the in-panel pink 'idle' regions use the same pattern as the legend idle swatch.
